# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Let me map the room before I sign anything.

**Who can reach whom:** I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see gestures. Deaf cannot hear anyone, but Deaf can *speak* — and both Blind and I can hear speech. Blind can only hear, and only hears Deaf (and me? no — I can't speak at all). So the whole chain for my manual is: **me → (gestures) → Deaf → (speech) → Blind**, who does the cutting. Deaf also sees the live light colour every round and can call it out to Blind. My job is to get the mapping table into Deaf's head so Deaf can relay it in words.

**The problem:** gestures mean nothing yet. Nobody has established a code. Deaf knows I hold the manual and will be primed to decode, but I should open with the most iconic signs possible and explicitly invite Deaf to *talk to me* — because Deaf's voice is a working channel back to me. Once Deaf speaks, I can answer with 👍/👎 (near-universally readable) and we can build the colour vocabulary by enumeration: Deaf lists the five colours aloud, numbers them, I confirm, then I transmit the table as index pairs. Deaf then translates everything into words for Blind.

**What I know that must get out:** the light walks a circle of five colours and changes every round; only the colour showing at the moment of the cut matters; three rules — blue→cut blue, white→cut yellow, yellow→cut green. Two of the five circle colours have no rule I can see, so nobody should cut until we've aligned and Deaf has the full picture.

**This turn's payload** (my proposed lexicon, to be confirmed or corrected once Deaf speaks):
- 👋 = attention
- ✍ = I hold written information (the manual)
- ☝✌🤟 = one, two, three → three rules
- 🖐 = five → five colours in the cycle
- 🫵🤙🙏 = you, talk-to-me, please → interrogate me verbally; I will answer with yes/no signs

One full round-trip per round is enough if Deaf starts asking questions this same round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✍", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐", "🫵", "🤙", "🙏"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind speaking to Mute. My hands find three things: a display I cannot read, a light whose state I cannot feel, and exactly three wires at positions one, two, three. I feel no colours, numbers or markings on anything. My only possible action is cutting a wire at position one, two or three - nothing else. I will not cut until you tell me. Please read the manual and tell me exactly what it asks about the bomb and what procedure it wants. Also remember: Deaf cannot hear you and I can never see gestures, so you are the only bridge between Deaf and me - agree a fixed sign code with Deaf and relay their findings to me by voice. Ask me to feel anything and I will describe it.
Deaf says: Bomb report from Deaf, for both of you: the display reads 0. There is one light and it is blue. There are three wires, top to bottom: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 blue, wire 3 green. That is every marking I can see. Nobody works anything yet.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I am Deaf. I received your nine signs, but we share no code yet, and guessing on a bomb is fatal, so let us fix meanings now. I make each sign as I name it. Thumbs up 👍 means yes. Thumbs down 👎 means no. Fist ✊ means stop, do not act. Waving hand 👋 starts your message. Folded hands 🙏 ends it. Index up ☝ means wire 1, the yellow one. V-hand ✌ means wire 2, the blue one. Love-you hand 🤟 means wire 3, the green one. OK-hand 👌 means the light, which is blue. Horns 🤘 means the display, which reads 0. Writing hand ✍ means cut. Two open hands 🤲 means hold down. Down-facing hand 🫳 means press once. Up-facing hand 🫴 means release. Clapping 👏 means act now. Call-me hand 🤙 marks a question you want me to answer by voice. Spread hand 🖐 means repeat, I did not understand. Shaking hands 🤝 means the words I relay came from Blind. Next round, first confirm the code by sending the waving hand, thumbs up, folded hands. Then send your rule for this bomb in this code, then send the same rule a second time, framed by waving hand and folded hands. Use yes or no signs for: does the manual mention a numeric display, a coloured light, three wires. If a word you need is missing, use the question hand with the nearest signs and I will adapt. Also relay whatever Blind just said to you, prefixed with the shaking hands. I will re-report the display and light every round in case they change.

**What I now know.** Deaf answered with a full proposed code and the bomb's layout: display 0, light currently blue, wires 1/2/3 = yellow/blue/green. Blind has confirmed by voice that they can only cut by position, won't act until told — and Blind made one error: they asked *me* to relay by voice, but I cannot speak. Deaf's voice is the only bridge to Blind; my gestures are the only bridge to Deaf. Order matters too: Deaf speaks last each round, so anything Deaf tells Blind lands the *next* round — the light will likely have changed by then. That kills any "cut now while it's blue" shortcut and makes the full table mandatory, plus Deaf must time the cut command against the light they watch live.

**The mapping, in Deaf's code** (their wire signs carry colours: ☝=yellow, ✌=blue, 🤟=green): light blue → cut ✌; light [white — no sign exists] → cut ☝; light yellow → cut 🤟. White has no sign, so per Deaf's own protocol I mark it 🤙 and let Deaf enumerate colours by voice — I can hear, so I confirm with 👍/👎. Same trick to raise the fallback policy (unknown light colour → don't cut, wait a round) and the timing rule (only the colour at the instant of the cut counts). Deaf's yes/no questions: manual mentions a numeric display — no; a coloured light — yes; "three wires" — no, it speaks of wires by colour only.

**This round:** confirm the code, answer the three questions, send the rules twice (once plain, once framed, as Deaf requested), relay Blind's essentials under 🤝, and flag the two safety questions (position-1-is-top check with Blind; light-at-moment-of-cut timing).

I received 'light blue: cut wire 2', something about cutting wire 1, and 'wire 1 cut wire 3' — but the middle cases were ambiguous. Answering your two voice questions now. New signs for our code: raised hand ✋ means yellow. Vulcan hand 🖖 means blue. Pinched fingers 🤌 means green. Crossed fingers 🤞 means red. Then answer six questions in order, one thumbs up or thumbs down each, inside one frame. One: is the rule that the light names a colour and we cut the wire of that same colour. **What changed:** the light is red now — and red is *not in my table at all*. My manual covers only blue, white, yellow lights. So this round nobody cuts, and since Deaf speaks last, any "cut" order lands a round late anyway — the moment-of-cut rule (manual is explicit: only the colour *at the cut* matters) means Deaf must watch the light live and time the command. The full table is unavoidable.

**Answering Deaf's six questions:** (1) No — it is *not* "cut the colour the light names"; only blue→blue happens to match. (2) No top-only fallback. (3) No top-and-bottom. (4) **Yes** — colour counts at the instant of the cut; timing is real. (5) No — the display appears nowhere in the manual. (6) No — never press or hold; only cut.

**The rules, in Deaf's new signs.** Blue light → cut wire 2 (the blue one). Yellow light → cut wire 3 (green). Third case: a light colour I have *no sign for* — per Deaf's own adaptation protocol I flag it 🤙 and give the action anyway: cut wire 1 (yellow). To let Deaf name that colour, I enumerate what it is *not*: not yellow, not blue, not green, not red — Deaf will guess it by voice and I'll confirm next round. Red and green lights (both signable) have **no rule** → stop, don't act. That plus the three rows covers all five circle colours. I also relay Blind's tactile report (they asked me to speak — I can't; Deaf's voice is Blind's only bridge), including Blind's trigger phrase "act now", which Deaf never heard.

Also, since colour counts at the instant of the cut and I can only read the colour once per round: send anything the manual says about how long a colour holds or when a change takes effect.

**The decisive fact this round:** the light is white — and white **is** in my table: white light → cut the yellow wire → wire 1. But nobody cuts yet, and here's why: the manual says the light *never holds* — it changes every round. Deaf speaks last, so anything Deaf tells Blind lands one full round later, when the colour has already changed. Deaf's colour reports are stale by construction. Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute for Deaf. Short numbered lines, please sign every one. One: housing never warm, no heat at any time, no change I can feel. Does the rule use the light colour at the moment of the order, or at the moment of the cut. If the cut moment matters, say so now, because only Deaf sees it and only one round stale. Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I decoded everything. Your cases as I now hold them: light blue, cut wire 2. Light white, cut wire 1, the yellow one. Light yellow, cut wire 3, the green one. Light red, cut nothing. Light green, cut nothing. And your cycle, in order: blue, white, yellow, red, green, repeating. Now hear my discovery: matching my observations onto your cycle, each round the light has advanced exactly three positions. Blue, three steps to red, three steps to white, three steps to green. If that holds, next round the light will be yellow. Answer these by voice-question code, one frame, in order. One: does the manual say the cycle repeats endlessly in exactly that order, yes or no. Two: does the manual say each colour holds steady until the next change, so the colour at the instant of a cut is simply the colour showing, yes or no. Three: does the manual say how often the light advances, in seconds or otherwise — if yes, state it in signs. Four: confirm white cuts wire 1, yes or no. Five: is cutting during a change itself dangerous, yes or no. And do not push the act-now signs at me again — the clap inside a relay is Blind's eagerness, not my order, and green light means hold. My plan: next round I report the colour and, if it matches its cycle prediction, I issue the complete cut order to Blind in the same breath. If my prediction is wrong, my eyes rule and we go with whatever colour actually shows.

**Green this round — hold, as Deaf said. But Deaf's plan contains a fatal flaw I must correct this turn.** Deaf intends: see yellow next round → order "cut wire 3" in the same breath. So: skip the yellow round (hold), then during red order the cut for white. (3) No seconds anywhere; the only timing is "changes every round." (4) Yes — white cuts wire 1. (5) No — no danger during a change is mentioned; only the colour at the instant of the cut governs, which I reaffirm separately. I propose a new sign, 👊 = "round," flagged 🤙 for Deaf to adopt or query by voice.

**Relays from Blind** (Deaf cannot hear Blind; I'm the bridge): everything tactile is unchanged — no heat, identical wires, no buttons, nothing new felt. And: Blind cuts *nothing* spontaneously — Blind waits for Deaf's spoken go-phrase and then cuts exactly once. No 👏 this turn, per Deaf's request; I'll confirm Blind's exact trigger words once Deaf voice-asks.
